turns.text: The tomatoes from Dad's plants came in this week. I picked the first ones on Sunday, which is when he used to call.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: Those first tomatoes arriving on Sunday must have brought your dad close—and made his absence feel sharper, too. You’ve been caring for his plants through all this, and that’s a tender way of keeping a connection with him. What was it like picking them?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: It was sad. I kept thinking I should call him and tell him they were ready. But they smelled really good, and for a minute I could almost hear what he’d say.

turns.speaker: helper

turns.speaker: user

turns.speaker: helper

turns.text: I don't know. I don't really want to turn it into a whole thing. Maybe I could just eat one and think of him.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds like enough. You don’t have to make it a whole thing—just eating one and thinking of him can be a quiet way to share the moment. Which one did you try first?

turns.speaker: helper

turns.text: A little, yeah. But then I remembered I can't tell him about it, and that hit me again.

turns.speaker: helper
